title: State of AI Geography
dek_2026: Where AI's money, compute, models, users and state programmes sit - the United States, China, Europe, India, the Gulf and the rest - measured with dated, sourced, confidence-rated figures for 2024, 2025 and 2026 to date.

2024: Stanford HAI's 2025 AI Index counted $109.1 billion of US private AI investment in 2024, nearly 12 times China's $9.3 billion and 24 times the UK's $4.5 billion.
US institutions released 40 notable AI models in 2024, against 15 from China and 3 from Europe, according to Stanford HAI's 2025 AI Index.
In January 2024 the top US model led the top Chinese model by 9.26% on the Chatbot Arena leaderboard, according to Stanford HAI's 2025 AI Index.
China had 249 million generative AI users at the end of December 2024, according to the China Internet Network Information Center (CNNIC).
China was granted 74.2% of the world's AI patents in 2024, 97,206 of 131,121, against 12.1% for the United States, according to Stanford HAI's 2026 AI Index.
2025: US private AI investment reached $285.9 billion in 2025, more than 23 times China's $12.4 billion, according to Stanford HAI's 2026 AI Index.
US-headquartered companies raised $159 billion, or 79%, of the $202.3 billion invested in AI start-ups worldwide in 2025, according to Crunchbase.
The United States took about 72% of the AI computing capacity added worldwide in 2025, up from around 60% a year in 2022-2024, according to Epoch AI's chip-imports data.
China's generative AI users rose to 602 million in December 2025 from 249 million a year earlier, according to CNNIC.
Microsoft estimated that 16.3% of the world's working-age population used generative AI in the second half of 2025, ranging from 64.0% in the UAE to 28.3% in the United States.
2026: The top US model led the top Chinese model by 2.7% on the LMArena leaderboard in March 2026, according to Stanford HAI's 2026 AI Index, compared with 1.70% in February 2025.

Microsoft estimated that 18.8% of the world's working-age population used generative AI in June 2026, led by the UAE at 73.3%, with the United States at 33.0% and China at 17.5% on a measure that excludes several Chinese domestic tools.

The United States received 78% of the AI compute added worldwide in the first half of 2026 and holds 72.2% of all AI compute added since 2022, against 9.6% for China and 5.1% for the EU, according to Epoch AI.
China had more than 700 million generative AI users in June 2026, a penetration rate above 50%, according to a CNNIC report published on 29 September 2026.
European AI start-ups raised a record $23 billion in the first half of 2026, 55% of all venture funding in the region, according to Crunchbase data compiled for HumanX.

2024: In 2024 the geography of AI capital was already lopsided. Stanford HAI's 2025 AI Index put US private AI investment at $109.1 billion, against $9.3 billion in China and $4.5 billion in the United Kingdom. The US figure was up from $67.2 billion in 2023, while China's private total stayed in single digits. Those Chinese numbers exclude state guidance funds, which Stanford estimates had channelled about $184 billion into AI firms between 2000 and 2023, and the ¥344 billion semiconductor 'Big Fund III' registered in May 2024. Private and state money are different instruments, and the honest comparison for 2024 is that the US led decisively on private capital while China relied on public vehicles that do not appear in the headline tables.

On output, the US produced 40 notable AI models in 2024, China 15 and Europe 3 (Stanford HAI, 2025 AI Index). But the performance gap between the best models from each country was narrowing quickly. In January 2024 the top US model led the top Chinese model by 9.26% on the Chatbot Arena leaderboard; by February 2025 the lead was 1.70%. China dominated research volume in a different way: it was granted 74.2% of the world's AI patents in 2024, against 12.1% for the US, according to the 2026 AI Index. Patents measure volume, not influence, and the US kept the lead on the most-cited work.

Governments began building rather than only regulating. India's Cabinet approved the ₹10,372 crore (about $1.25 billion) IndiaAI Mission in March 2024; Abu Dhabi set up MGX; and Japan's METI subsidised domestic cloud compute. Nvidia's sovereign AI revenue for its fiscal 2025, roughly calendar 2024, was not disclosed, but its later statement that the business 'more than tripled' to over $30 billion implies a base under about $10 billion. Consumer adoption in China was still early: CNNIC counted 249 million generative AI users at the end of 2024, about 18% of the population.
2025: 2025 turned a large lead in private capital into an overwhelming one. Stanford HAI's 2026 AI Index put US private AI investment at $285.9 billion, 2.6 times the 2024 figure and 23 times China's $12.4 billion. On Stanford's global private total of $344.7 billion, that is an 82.9% US share by Report AI's calculation. Crunchbase's venture data agree: US companies raised $159 billion of the $202.3 billion that went to AI start-ups, 79%. Europe grew from a much smaller base, to about $17.5 billion of AI venture funding, and Mistral's valuation doubled to €11.7 billion. DeepSeek-R1's release in January 2025, and its brief tie with the top US model in February, showed that capital alone did not determine capability.

Compute concentrated even faster than money. Epoch AI estimates the US took 72% of the AI compute added worldwide in 2025, up from around 60% a year in 2022-2024. Export policy changed repeatedly. The AI Diffusion Rule issued in January 2025 was rescinded in May; a licence requirement on Nvidia's H20 in April led to a $4.5 billion charge; and by November Washington had approved the equivalent of 35,000 Blackwell GB300 chips each for Saudi Arabia's HUMAIN and the UAE's G42. On an analyst's customer-headquarters count, China's share of Nvidia revenue fell from about 19% in fiscal 2025 to 9.1% in fiscal 2026.

Adoption followed income and policy more closely than model origin. Microsoft estimated that 16.3% of the world's working-age population used generative AI in the second half of 2025, from 64.0% in the UAE and 60.9% in Singapore to 28.3% in the US, which ranked 24th. Anthropic's Economic Index found the US produced 21.6% of Claude.ai use, while Israel used it at seven times its population share. In China, CNNIC counted 602 million generative AI users by December, up 142% in a year, and 748 generative AI services had completed filing with the Cyberspace Administration. The flow of top AI talent into the US fell about 80% over the year to September 2025, according to the 2026 AI Index.
2026: The model gap between the US and China has largely closed and is now small enough to change sign. Stanford's 2026 AI Index put the top US model 2.7% ahead of the top Chinese model on LMArena in March 2026, slightly wider than the 1.70% of February 2025. On the Artificial Analysis index in September 2026, two Chinese models were in the global top four, within two points of the leader. The more durable difference is distribution: Chinese labs publish weights and US frontier labs do not. Chinese models accounted for 41% of Hugging Face downloads in the year to February 2026, and one VC estimate puts their share of OpenRouter tokens near 61% in May 2026.

Compute moved the other way. Epoch AI estimates the US received 78% of the AI compute added worldwide in the first half of 2026 and holds 72.2% of everything added since 2022, against 9.6% for China and 5.1% for the EU. Export controls loosened for chips and tightened for models. A January 2026 rule moved H200 exports to China to case-by-case licensing with a 25% charge, but Beijing held purchases back and H200 sales were under 1% of Nvidia's data-centre revenue in the quarter to July. In June, Commerce placed Anthropic's Claude Fable 5 and Mythos 5 under export controls; Anthropic suspended both on 12 June and restored them on 1 July after Commerce ended the order, with Mythos 5 limited to US organisations.

Capital remains American, with Europe accelerating. Crunchbase counted about $319 billion, roughly 88%, of AI start-up funding going to US-headquartered companies so far in 2026, a share swollen by a few very large rounds, including OpenAI's $122 billion raise. European AI start-ups raised $23 billion in the first half alone, more than in all of 2025, and Mistral was valued at over €21 billion in September. China's largest private raise came late: DeepSeek's reported $15-16 billion round in October, at a valuation reported between $74 billion and $90 billion. Stanford's country totals for 2026 will not be available until 2027.

Usage is spreading fastest outside the US. Microsoft's estimate of the share of working-age people using generative AI rose to 18.8% worldwide in June 2026, 73.3% in the UAE and 40.6% in South Korea, against 33.0% in the US. Microsoft's China figure, 17.5%, omits domestic tools; CNNIC counted more than 700 million Chinese users by June 2026, and Doubao alone reached 419 million monthly users by September. States are spending more but still modestly: South Korea's 2026 AI budget of about ₩10.1 trillion is triple 2025's, and India had onboarded 38,231 subsidised GPUs by March. None of these series is measured the same way across countries.

takeaways_2026: The model gap is nearly gone: the top US model led the top Chinese model by 2.7% on LMArena in March 2026 (Stanford HAI), and Chinese open-weight models now lead global download charts.
Money and machines are more concentrated, not less: about 88% of AI start-up funding so far in 2026 (Crunchbase) and 78% of new AI compute in H1 2026 (Epoch AI) went to the United States.
Usage leaders are small, rich and state-backed: the UAE (73.3%) and Singapore (64.3%) top Microsoft's June 2026 ranking, while the US sits 21st at 33.0%.

Export controls shifted from chips to models: H200 sales to China resumed under licence but stayed under 1% of Nvidia data-centre revenue, while two frontier US models were suspended under export controls from 12 June to 1 July 2026.
yoy_takeaways: US private AI investment rose from $109.1 billion in 2024 to $285.9 billion in 2025 while China's rose from $9.3 billion to $12.4 billion, widening the ratio from about 12x to 23x (Stanford HAI).
The US share of newly added AI compute climbed from about 60% (2024) to 72% (2025) to 78% (H1 2026), according to Epoch AI, even as China's share of AI patents and open-model downloads rose.
The US-China top-model gap fell from 9.26% (Jan 2024) to 1.70% (Feb 2025) and then held near parity at 2.7% (Mar 2026) on Chatbot Arena/LMArena (Stanford HAI).

China's generative AI user base grew from 249 million (Dec 2024) to 602 million (Dec 2025) to more than 700 million (Jun 2026), according to CNNIC, making it the largest national user base by that survey measure.

faq_2026.q: Which country leads in AI in 2026?
faq_2026.a: The United States leads on capital and compute: Stanford HAI's 2026 AI Index put US private AI investment at $285.9 billion in 2025, 23 times China's $12.4 billion, and Epoch AI estimates the US holds 72.2% of all AI compute added since 2022. China leads on AI patents (74.2% of grants in 2024), open-weight model downloads and the size of its domestic user base (more than 700 million generative AI users in June 2026, per CNNIC). On model performance the two are close: the top US model led by 2.7% on LMArena in March 2026.

faq_2026.q: How far behind the US is China in AI models?
faq_2026.a: Very little on headline benchmarks. Stanford HAI's 2026 AI Index found the top US model 2.7% ahead of the top Chinese model on the LMArena leaderboard in March 2026, compared with 9.26% in January 2024 and 1.70% in February 2025. On the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index in September 2026, Alibaba's Qwen3.8-Max scored 58 and Moonshot's Kimi K3 57.1 against 58.9 for OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol. The US still released more notable models in 2025: 50 or 59 against China's 30 or 35, depending on the edition of Epoch AI's data used.

faq_2026.q: Which countries use AI the most?
faq_2026.a: By Microsoft's estimate of the share of working-age people using generative AI, the UAE led in June 2026 at 73.3%, followed by Singapore at 64.3%, Ireland at 49.9% and France at 49.6%; South Korea was 12th at 40.6% and the United States 21st at 33.0%. The world average was 18.8%. Microsoft's China figure, 17.5%, excludes several domestic Chinese tools; China's own CNNIC survey counted more than 700 million generative AI users, over half the population, in June 2026.

faq_2026.q: How much of the world's AI compute is in the United States?
faq_2026.a: About three-quarters. Epoch AI's chip-imports data estimates the US received 72.2% of the AI compute (in H100-equivalents) added worldwide between 2022 and the second quarter of 2026, against 9.6% for China, 5.1% for the EU, 2.4% for Malaysia and 1.6% each for India and Japan. The US share of newly added compute rose from about 60% in 2024 to 72% in 2025 and 78% in the first half of 2026. China holds about 18% of chips but only about 10% of compute, because many of its chips are lower-performance.

faq_2026.q: Do US chip export controls still restrict China in 2026?
faq_2026.a: Yes, but the form has changed. A Commerce rule effective 15 January 2026 moved Nvidia H200 exports to China to case-by-case licensing with a 25% charge, but Chinese authorities discouraged purchases, and H200 sales to Chinese buyers were under 1% of Nvidia's data-centre revenue in the quarter to 26 July 2026 (Bloomberg). In June 2026 the controls reached models for the first time in practice, when Commerce placed Anthropic's Claude Fable 5 and Mythos 5 under export controls; both were suspended on 12 June and restored on 1 July, with Mythos 5 limited to US organisations.

stop_quoting.fact: 69.7% is China's 2023 share from the 2025 AI Index. The 2026 AI Index puts China at 74.2% of AI patents granted in 2024 (97,206 of 131,121), against 12.1% for the US.

stop_quoting.claim: 59% of the world's top AI researchers work in the United States.
stop_quoting.fact: That is MacroPolo's 2019 figure. Its 2022 data put the US share at 42% (ITIF reading) or 46% (Carnegie reading); MacroPolo ceased operations in 2025 and there is no later edition.

stop_quoting.claim: The US accounted for $285.9 billion of $581 billion of global AI investment in 2025.
stop_quoting.fact: $285.9 billion is US private AI investment; the matching global private total is $344.7 billion (an 82.9% US share). $581.7 billion is total corporate AI investment, a broader measure that includes M&A and minority stakes.

stop_quoting.claim: The US-China AI model gap is 1.7%.
stop_quoting.fact: 1.70% was the February 2025 reading. Stanford HAI's 2026 AI Index puts it at 2.7% in March 2026 on LMArena.

stop_quoting.claim: Only 17.5% of people in China use AI (Microsoft).
stop_quoting.fact: Microsoft's Q2 2026 figure excludes several widely used Chinese domestic tools. CNNIC counted more than 700 million generative AI users in China in June 2026, a penetration rate above 50%. The two measures are not comparable.
Mistranslation of 3.8 yi (380 million). QuestMobile put Doubao at 382 million monthly users in May 2026 and 419 million in Q3 2026.

stop_quoting.claim: The $500 billion Stargate project is US government AI spending.
stop_quoting.fact: Stargate is a private joint venture; the White House confirmed it involves no federal funds. Direct US federal AI R&D was a $3.3 billion request for FY2025.
